quote: Zariski recommended that Abhyankar attempt to extend local uniformization (and hence resolution of singularities) to positive characteristic
note: The problem was explicitly posed by Oscar Zariski to his doctoral student Shreeram Abhyankar in the early-to-mid 1950s (circa 1950-1954), framed as a research direction rather than a formal published problem statement. Zariski had discovered fundamental obstructions in positive characteristic (e.g., failure of Bertini's theorem) by 1944. The specific question was whether local uniformization, and hence resolution of singularities, could extend to positive characteristic—a natural question after Zariski's characteristic-zero results. Abhyankar solved surfaces in positive characteristic in 1956.
